headline: Founder-led education and Wisconsin-rooted paid messaging are still the clearest growth levers, but this week’s biggest business risk is stale reporting while the category gets sharper around premium, snackable, and protein-forward frozen occasions.

items: Paid efficiency still has clear winners: Meta's 'Straight From Wisconsin' remains the volume leader at 13,622 link clicks and $0.11 CPC, while 'Meet Real Dough Pizza Co.' is still one of the most efficient ads at 4.67% CTR.

Founder/operator content still earns the most trust: Founder Pro Tips remains the top Instagram post and top Facebook reel, with additional backfill this week despite no true reporting-window advance.
Bottom-funnel demand still looks healthy when intent is high: Google branded search continues to deliver 5.68% CTR at $0.21 CPC, and Instagram website clicks edged up again to 1,273.
The June 12 Whatagraph pull succeeded technically, but the trusted Meta/Google/Facebook/Instagram window is still stuck at 2026-05-12. This is not a true weekly close.
Competitor Google search is still the weakest paid pocket: $1,227.77 spent at $0.59 CPC versus branded search at $0.21 CPC.

This week's market intel shows the freezer aisle getting more competitive on three fronts at once: premium craft claims (Palermo/Connie's, Di Fara), private-label/value pressure (Aldi, Walmart), and snackable/protein-forward expansion (Hot Pockets, Farm Rich, David, Hero Bread, Kodiak).
There is still no usable Real Dough review feed and no current Real Dough operations snapshot, so sentiment and operational risk are under-instrumented right when competition is accelerating.
REPORTING: Fix the Whatagraph freshness issue before next Friday so leadership is reviewing a real post-May-12 performance window instead of attribution backfill noise.

PAID + CREATIVE: Keep 'Straight From Wisconsin' and founder-led education as controls, then brief the agency to build the next round around fermentation proof, ingredient reassurance, and practical dinner utility.
SEARCH: Cap or trim competitor terms unless conversion proof justifies the premium; branded and sourdough-intent traffic remain materially cleaner.

CATEGORY RESPONSE: Test at least one creative angle around flexible occasions or premium snackability without abandoning the core family-dinner positioning, because the aisle is clearly expanding beyond classic meal-only framing.
DATA COVERAGE: Stand up a usable Real Dough review/sentiment feed and current ops snapshot so next week's summary is not blind on customer voice and retail execution.

agency_brief.what_worked: Specific beats generic. Wisconsin-rooted messaging, founder/operator voice, fermentation/process proof, and easy-dinner reassurance continue to outperform broad premium language.
agency_brief.what_didnt: Competitor search remains expensive, vague premium positioning is still too soft, and the stale reporting window makes false week-over-week storytelling easy.
agency_brief.recommendation: Keep the creative system tight: founder education, sourdough/process credibility, ingredient trust, and dinner-solve utility. Add one exploratory lane that speaks to premium snackable or flexible freezer occasions, because category innovation is clustering there.
agency_brief.competitive_context: This week reinforced a three-way category squeeze: established brands are extending into snack-sized formats, challenger brands are pushing protein-forward frozen products, and premium/regional pizza players keep sharpening craft claims. Real Dough's moat should stay centered on authentic sourdough craft, Wisconsin credibility, and retailer-ready execution.

missing: No usable review sentiment feed for Real Dough. data/reviews.json still contains place-not-found errors for other MSHG brands, not Real Dough customer feedback.
No current-week Real Dough operations data. data/operations/ still contains older Merriment snapshots from March/April, not current Real Dough operating inputs.
stale: The latest trustworthy analytics view is still YTD through 2026-05-12, not a clean current-week slice.
Week-over-week Meta and Google movement is effectively frozen because the source reporting window did not advance.
anomalies: YouTube and TikTok tabs in the current Whatagraph export are still returning sample/demo data, so live video-platform ranking remains excluded.
The small Instagram and Facebook changes versus last week appear to be late organic backfills inside the same reporting window, not a fresh performance shift.
